profile.summary: ProGen2 is a suite of autoregressive protein language models released by Salesforce Research, in sizes from 151M to 6.4B parameters. Given a start token or the beginning of a sequence, a model generates amino acids one at a time, so it can write new sequences; the same model also scores an existing sequence by its log-likelihood, which the authors use to predict protein fitness without any fine-tuning. The checkpoints differ in the sequence database they were trained on, which includes genomic, metagenomic and immune repertoire sources.
profile.summary_source_locator: arXiv abstract; README: title, Models, Setup

summary_quotes.text: We introduce a suite of protein language models, named ProGen2, that are scaled up to 6.4B parameters and trained on different sequence datasets drawn from over a billion proteins from genomic, metagenomic, and immune repertoire databases.
generating novel viable sequences, and predicting protein fitness without additional finetuning
Official release of the **ProGen2** models (`151M`, `764M`, `2.7B`, `6.4B`) for **Protein Engineering**

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each ProGen2 checkpoint is a decoder-only transformer trained to predict the next token in a protein sequence. The configuration class in the repository sets the shape of a model: vocabulary, context positions, embedding width, number of layers and number of attention heads. Generation is done by the sampling script, which encodes a context string with the model's tokenizer and samples continuations with a temperature and nucleus (top-p) setting. The repository also ships a likelihood script that scores a given sequence. In the README's examples, a sequence is written between the tokens 1 and 2, and free generation starts from the token 1 alone.
sections.source_locator: configuration_progen.py: ProGenConfig; sample.py: argument defaults, sample(); README: Setup

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Seven checkpoints are published: progen2-small (151M), progen2-medium, progen2-oas and progen2-base (764M each), progen2-large and progen2-BFD90 (2.7B each) and progen2-xlarge (6.4B). They are downloaded as tar.gz archives from a Google Storage bucket; there is no official Hugging Face repository in the sources read, and the archives are not versioned by a revision hash. A result must therefore name the checkpoint, and should also record the sampling settings, because the script's defaults (temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, max length 256, fp16 on GPU) differ from the values in the README's example command.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Autoregressive (decoder-only) protein language model, used for sequence generation and for zero-shot fitness prediction by log-likelihood.

quotes.text: predicting protein fitness without additional finetuning

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer with the ProGen configuration: the class defaults are 28 layers, embedding width 4096, 16 attention heads and a vocabulary of 50400. Per-checkpoint shapes are not listed in the sources read.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A context string tokenised by the model's own tokenizer: either the single start token 1 for free generation, or a partial or complete amino-acid sequence framed by the tokens 1 and 2.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated amino-acid sequences from the sampling script, and a log-likelihood for a supplied sequence from the likelihood script.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 151M (progen2-small), 764M (progen2-medium, progen2-oas, progen2-base), 2.7B (progen2-large, progen2-BFD90), 6.4B (progen2-xlarge), as the README's table states.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Different sequence datasets per checkpoint, drawn from over a billion proteins from genomic, metagenomic and immune repertoire databases. Which database belongs to which checkpoint is not stated in the sources read; the names oas and BFD90 are not explained in the README.

quotes.text: trained on different sequence datasets drawn from over a billion proteins from genomic, metagenomic, and immune repertoire databases

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Seven checkpoints: progen2-small, progen2-medium, progen2-oas, progen2-base, progen2-large, progen2-BFD90 and progen2-xlarge. No later ProGen2 revisions are named in the sources read.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not reported. The sources read do not date the training databases; the paper was released in June 2022 and only its abstract was read.
facts.source_locator: README, all sections; arXiv abstract page

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 2048 positions in the configuration class default (n_positions and n_ctx); the README's sampling example sets a maximum generated length of 1024, and the script's own default is 256. No per-checkpoint context length is given.

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Code: https://github.com/salesforce/progen (the progen2 directory). Weights: tar.gz archives under https://storage.googleapis.com/sfr-progen-research/checkpoints/, for example progen2-large.tar.gz, downloaded with wget. No gating and no login are mentioned.

strengths.text: Code and models are BSD-3 licensed, and the weights download directly from a public bucket without an account.

quotes.text: Our code and models are BSD-3 licensed.

strengths.text: Four sizes from 151M to 6.4B let a user trade accuracy against hardware.
The same checkpoint does both jobs: the repository ships a sampling script for generation and a likelihood script for scoring an existing sequence, with no fine-tuning in between.

quotes.text: predicting protein fitness without additional finetuning

strengths.text: Checkpoints trained on different databases are published side by side, including an immune repertoire model (progen2-oas), so a user can pick the one matching their protein family.

limitations.text: The pinned dependencies are old: torch 1.9.0+cu111, transformers 4.16.2 and tokenizers 0.10.3, and the setup uses python3.8.
The weights are plain tar.gz archives on a storage bucket with no revision hash, so a run can only be pinned by checkpoint name, not by a verified version.
The scripts assume a CUDA device and fp16 by default, falling back to CPU and fp32; the sources read do not state the GPU memory needed for the 6.4B checkpoint.
The authors ask for care in how generated sequences are used, and for oversight during design and deployment.

quotes.text: care should be taken in terms of the end use-cases of these designed samples and downstream effects to ensure safe, non-nefarious, and ethical applications

run_guide.summary: Set up the ProGen2 repository at a pinned commit, download one checkpoint and generate two sequences with it.
prerequisites: python3.8, as the README's virtual environment step uses it.
The pinned dependencies are torch 1.9.0+cu111, transformers 4.16.2 and tokenizers 0.10.3, so a CUDA 11.1 compatible setup is assumed. The script falls back to CPU and fp32 if no CUDA device is found.
Disk space for the checkpoint archive and its extracted contents. Code and models are BSD-3 licensed.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/salesforce/progen
cd progen
git checkout --detach c27a419c234a0997923761e1fe7daffcebf0eaf5
cd progen2
steps.explanation: The README's clone and cd lines, with a checkout line added to get the repository at the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Download and extract a checkpoint
steps.shell:
model=progen2-large
wget -P checkpoints/${model} https://storage.googleapis.com/sfr-progen-research/checkpoints/${model}.tar.gz
tar -xvf checkpoints/${model}/${model}.tar.gz -C checkpoints/${model}/
steps.explanation: The README's checkpoint step, unchanged. progen2-large is 2.7B parameters; replace the model name with another row of the README's table for a smaller or larger checkpoint.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
python3.8 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip3 install --upgrade pip setuptools
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
steps.explanation: The README's virtual environment step, unchanged. It installs the pinned torch, transformers and tokenizers versions.

steps.title: Generate two sequences
steps.explanation: The README's sampling command, unchanged. It samples two continuations from the start token at temperature 0.8 and top-p 0.9, up to 1024 tokens. To score an existing sequence instead, the README gives a likelihood.py command with the sequence framed by the tokens 1 and 2.

outputs: The sampling script prints the context and then the generated sequences. The likelihood script prints a log-likelihood for the supplied sequence; the sources read do not show its exact output format.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The dependency pins are from 2022 (torch 1.9.0+cu111, python3.8) and may not install on current hardware or CUDA versions.
The checkpoint archive has no published checksum or revision in the sources read.
progen2-large is 2.7B parameters; the sources read do not state how much GPU memory it or progen2-xlarge needs.

quotes.text: Our code and models are BSD-3 licensed.

notes: context_length is null in the structured rows because the only figure, 2048, is the configuration class default, not a per-checkpoint value; the README's own example caps generation at 1024 tokens. Parameter counts are the README's rounded figures (151M, 764M, 2.7B, 6.4B). Hugging Face holds many progen2 repositories, all third-party uploads or fine-tunes; the official weights are tar.gz archives on a Google Storage bucket. Only the arXiv abstract was read, so per-checkpoint training data is not described.
